title: 11 km down, the ocean presses 8 tons on every square inch

beats.say: At the bottom of the ocean, 11 kilometres down, the water presses 8 tons on every square inch.
beats.speak: At the bottom of the ocean, eleven kilometres down, the water presses eight tons on every square inch.

head: WHY THAT
NUMBER?
beats.say: NOAA says every 10.06 metres of seawater adds one more atmosphere of pressure. So let's take a balloon down and watch.
beats.speak: Noah says every ten point zero six metres of seawater adds one more atmosphere of pressure. So let's take a balloon down and watch.

head: JUST 10 METRES
DOWN.
beats.say: Just 10 metres down, the pressure doubles to 2 atmospheres. The balloon is squeezed to half its volume.
beats.speak: Just ten metres down, the pressure doubles to two atmospheres. The balloon is squeezed to half its volume.

head: NOW 1,000
METRES DOWN.
beats.say: At 1,000 metres it's 100 atmospheres. The air in the balloon is squeezed to about 1% of its volume.
beats.speak: At one thousand metres it's a hundred atmospheres. The air in the balloon is squeezed to about one percent of its volume.

head: FOAM CUPS
SHRINK HERE.
beats.say: NOAA scientists send foam cups down this deep. The pressure crushes the air out of the foam, and they come back shrunk.
beats.speak: Noah scientists send foam cups down this deep. The pressure crushes the air out of the foam, and they come back shrunk.

head: THE TITANIC
IS DEEPER.
beats.say: The Titanic lies 12,500 feet down, 3,810 metres. That's 380 atmospheres: 2.8 tons on every square inch.
beats.speak: The Titanic lies twelve thousand five hundred feet down, three thousand eight hundred and ten metres. That's three hundred and eighty atmospheres: two point eight tons on every square inch.

head: NOW THE DEEPEST
SPOT ON EARTH.
beats.say: Challenger Deep: 10,935 metres. 1,088 atmospheres. 8 tons on every square inch of you.
beats.speak: Challenger Deep: ten thousand nine hundred and thirty five metres. One thousand and eighty eight atmospheres. Eight tons on every square inch of you.

head: DROP EVEREST
IN THE HOLE.
beats.say: Drop Mount Everest in, all 8,848.86 metres of it. Its summit would still sit 2,086 metres underwater.
beats.speak: Drop Mount Everest in, all eight thousand eight hundred and forty eight point eight six metres of it. Its summit would still sit two thousand and eighty six metres underwater.

head: AND STILL,
LIFE.
beats.say: Reality check: even at 8 tons per square inch, NOAA says life exists down there.
beats.speak: Reality check: even at eight tons per square inch, Noah says there is still life down there.

beats.say: Follow Ship With Pip for more.

caption: Every 10.06 m of seawater adds one atmosphere of pressure (NOAA). Take a balloon down: at 10 m it is squeezed to half its volume, at 1,000 m (100 atmospheres) to about 1%. NOAA scientists shrink foam cups at that depth. The Titanic lies at 12,500 ft, 3,810 m: 380 atmospheres, 2.8 tons per square inch. Challenger Deep, 10,935 m: 1,088 atmospheres, 8 tons on every square inch. Drop Everest in and 2,086 m of water would still sit over its summit. And life still lives down there. Balloon volumes use Boyle's law at constant temperature; tons are US tons of 2,000 lb.
notes: m_per_atm 10.06 and psi_atm 14.7: NOAA NOS, 'For every 33 feet (10.06 meters) you go down, the pressure increases by one atmosphere'; surface air '14.7 pounds per square inch (1 bar)'. WHOI agrees: 'For every 10 meters of water, hydrostatic pressure increases by one atmosphere' and at 10 m 'the pressure is double'.

cup_m 1000: NOAA Ocean Explorer (12midatlantic, Sept 30): 'The colored cups were sent down on the CTD to a depth of about 1,000 meters' and 'the pressure of the water squeezes and shrinks the cups'. Deepeast01: 'substantial shrinkage as the air in the styrofoam is compressed'. No shrink fraction is sourced, so none is stated; the on-screen cup shrink is illustrative only.
titanic_ft 12500: CBS News, 'The Titanic wreckage, which is about 12,500 feet deep'. ft_m 0.3048 exact definition.

deep_m 10935: Live Science, 'about 35,876 feet (10,935 meters) deep'. Guinness via Live Science: pressure 'more than 1,000 times' sea level; WHOI 'In the deepest trenches, it's 1,100 times greater'; EarthDate 'more than 8 tons per square inch'. Our 1,088 atm and 8.0 tons/sq in are consistent.
Life: CBS News, 'The pressure in the trench is 8 tons per square inch, but still, life exists, NOAA says.'
everest_m 8848.86: NPR, 'the summit now stands precisely at 8,848.86 meters'.
lb_ton 2000: US short ton definition (the tons in the EarthDate and CBS NOAA figure are US tons per square inch).

Pressures are absolute (1 atm of air plus 1 atm per 10.06 m). Balloon volume fraction = 1/p (Boyle's law, constant temperature, ideal gas; at 100 atm air is close to ideal). vol_cup 0.00996 drives the drawn balloon size.
Constant 1: one atmosphere per step, and 'about 1%' is vol_cup_pct 0.996 rounded.
